title: Make Settings navigation retain the active category

messages.text: When I open Settings, choose Appearance, close it, and reopen it, it always returns to General. Can we retain the last category for the current application session?
I’ll trace the page state and opening action first.

tools.name: search
tools.label: Find settings page state
tools.output: Found settings state in src/settings.rs and page creation in src/update/settings.rs.

messages.text: The active category is currently view-local, so reopening constructs General again.
Current application session only. I do not want this becoming a persisted preference.
Understood. I’ll keep it in application state and avoid changing the settings file format.

tools.name: read
tools.label: Inspect app state
tools.output: AppState owns session-lifetime UI state. Preferences serialize separately through Settings.

messages.text: Check that opening a file or switching tabs cannot reset it accidentally.
I inspected the tab and runtime paths. They do not rebuild AppState, so session state is a suitable home.

tools.name: read
tools.label: Inspect unrelated navigation paths
tools.output: Read-only inspection; no settings category mutation found.

messages.text: I’ll add an optional active category to session state, initialized lazily when Settings is first opened.
Will it behave sensibly if a category is removed in a later build?
Yes. The state stores the catalog enum, and opening validates it against the active catalog before falling back to General.

tools.name: read
tools.label: Inspect settings catalog
tools.output: Category is an enum with stable display metadata and a General default.

messages.text: Please make keyboard selection update it too, not just mouse clicks.
The category action already funnels mouse and keyboard through one message, so I’ll update state in that handler.

tools.name: patch
tools.label: Add session category state
tools.output: Changed AppState, settings update handler, messages, and settings view.

messages.text: Could the heading say which category is active on a narrow screen? The sidebar may be collapsed.
I’ll use the existing category metadata for the compact heading, so the label has one source of truth.

tools.name: test
tools.label: Run focused settings tests
tools.output:
FAILED: expected Appearance after reopen, got General
This is the test before wiring the reopen action.

messages.text: Good catch. Please wire reopening through the same resolver, then rerun.
The initial patch updated selection but not construction. I’ll route construction through the stored-or-default resolver.

tools.name: patch
tools.label: Use stored category when opening Settings
tools.output: OpenSettings now resolves last_settings_category before constructing the page.

messages.text: Does closing Settings preserve state if a modal is open above it?
Yes. The modal stack closes the surface but does not mutate session state. I added a regression case for it.

tools.name: patch
tools.label: Add settings reopen tests
tools.output: Added mouse, keyboard, modal-close, and invalid-category fallback cases.

messages.text: Please make sure we do not serialize this in the existing config round trip.
The field is in AppState only. I’ll add an explicit round-trip assertion to protect that boundary.
Can you also check the category list stays reachable with a short window?
I’ll use the existing narrow-window fixture and keep the navigation scrollable.

tools.name: git_diff
tools.label: Inspect pending changes
tools.output: 17 files changed; settings state, navigation rendering, tests, fixture, and documentation are included. Existing runtime and editor files were inspected only.

messages.text: The scope seems fair. Don’t add counters or any migration messaging to the settings UI.
No extra UI copy or persisted migration is included.
Show a narrow screenshot and then we can stop there.
I’m checking that the compact heading and category list agree at 420px.

tools.name: run_fixture
tools.label: Exercise narrow Settings view
tools.output:
Active category: Appearance
Navigation remains scrollable
No horizontal overflow

messages.text: That is enough. Please include a brief UI note for future maintainers.
I’ll document that the active category is session UI state, not a preference.

tools.name: patch
tools.label: Document category lifetime
tools.output: Added a concise note beside Settings navigation behavior.

messages.text: Looks good for review.
Ready for review. This fictional fixture intentionally has no annotations, change counters, or commit correlation.
